author: github-actions
title: CASE FILE — The Idle Browser
subtitle: 20:25 UTC on main, and Steel taught its browsers to wait without wasting a heartbeat.
act1_title: Too Many Engines, Not Enough Roads
when_where: July 24th, 20:25 UTC. Main branch, the night the dashboard looked like a traffic jam. Every new job spun up a fresh Chrome, burned a fresh set of resources, and died alone when the run was over. Sessions scattered across logs, files living off to the side, operators juggling tabs like flaming knives.
who_whom: Steel versus its own creation. On one side, the cluster bill — swollen with short‑lived browsers that never learned to share. On the other, a quiet idea in the release notes: reuse idle browsers when the config is unchanged, teach them to keep state, expose a files API, and give every run a session details endpoint so the humans can finally see what the agents are doing.
what_why: With v0.2.0‑beta, the browser stops being disposable hardware and starts acting like a character with memory. Idle instances are reused instead of discarded, the new files API turns scratch data into something you can point to, and the session details endpoint hands operators a clean dossier for every run. Steel isn’t just running Chrome anymore; it’s running a precinct full of browsers that know when to stay, when to leave, and where the evidence lives.
verdict: They didn’t just cut costs; they gave every browser a badge and a filing cabinet, then asked it to testify on what the agents saw.
